Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.

result.rule: Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Do not merge separately described actions into one task or split one stated action without a process reason. Preserve described dependencies.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Keep catch and throw direction consistent and avoid representing one occurrence redundantly as an equivalent adjacent task and event.

result.rule: When the description states an activity as a verb and object, followed by a purpose, scope or qualifying clause in the same sentence: Name the task with the verb and object of the stated activity, using the description's own words, and leave the purpose or scope clause out of the task label. Do not append words from that clause, and do not add a qualifier the description does not attach to the activity itself.

When the description states several distinct items of the same kind in one sentence, joined by commas or 'or' or 'and', and each item is described as something a participant performs or receives: model each listed item as its own task with a short verb-object label, placed in the sequence the sentence implies, instead of merging the items into one task whose label names all of them

When the description states one activity performed on an object, and a clause in the same sentence (for example introduced by 'to' or 'for') lists several distinct aspects, checks or assessments joined by commas and 'and': Model each listed aspect, check or assessment as its own task, in the order the description states them, connected by sequence flows. Do not merge them into one task whose label lists all of them. Keep each task label to the verb and one aspect, using the description's own words, and do not turn the purpose clause into a single combined label.

When The description states that a participant itself performs an action (for example selecting, providing, or sending something) as a step of the process, rather than the information arriving from another party.: Model that action as a task labeled with the verb the description uses for the participant's action, and keep the label to that verb and its main object. Do not use a receive label, and do not add detail the description does not attach to the action. Use a receive task or a message event only when the description says the information arrives from another party.
